evidence: Thin ﬁlms of VO2 were deposited on soda glass, measuring about 1–6 cm2 in area. The substrates, after cleaning, were replaced on a graphite susceptor, whose temperature was varied in the range 400–4751C using the halogen lamps. The precursor was kept in a heated vaporizer and the vapours were carried to the reaction zone using argon as the carrier gas. The precursor vapours, reacting gas (O2) and the purge gas (Ar) were admitted in pulses through air actuated pneumatic valves capable of operating at temperatures up to 2001C.
